Shoelaces from the shoemaker – Like in the old days, now online

As a master shoemaker, I know that a shoe is only as good as its fit. At LACCICO you will find waxed shoelaces made to traditional standards in family manufactories in Italy and Poland. Carefully braided, tear-resistant and full of character – for shoes that make history. Here you will find answers to the most frequent questions about our quality and range.
Expertise & origin

Behind LACCICO there is no anonymous mass product, but the decades of experience of master shoemaker Alexander Breitenbach. Following the motto “Shoelaces from the shoemaker – like in the old days, now online”, I select every model according to strict craft criteria.


Our partner manufactories in Italy and Poland look back on a family tradition that has grown over generations. In Tuscany in particular, we draw on the deep-rooted know-how of a region that has been the centre of the European leather and shoe trade for centuries. The result is shoelaces that are full of character, tear-resistant and of high quality – just as you would expect from a master shoemaker.

The decisive difference lies in the details of production and the depth of the material. While cheap producers often rely on loose hollow braids, the quality at LACCICO comes from a careful ratio of yarn thickness and number of braiding bobbins to the specific requirements of each lace.


Our laces are made on classic machines in such a way that a densely braided, shape-retaining lace is created. Through close exchange with experts from the Italian shoe manufacturing trade, we make sure that every braid structure is matched to the respective type of shoe. With LACCICO you choose a product that not only looks better, but also feels better thanks to its grippy and supple feel.

detailsSettings.label: What sets LACCICO apart from mass-produced goods?

text.htmlDescription: Product construction & quality

The quality of a LACCICO shoelace begins at its core. Unlike loosely braided standard laces, we rely on a highly compact braid. On modern braiding machines, this creates a densely braided structure that makes the lace exceptionally shape-retaining and tear-resistant. The result is a product that keeps its shape even under high tensile load and does not stretch out.

detailsSettings.label: What makes the braid structure so special?

text.htmlDescription: For us, waxing is not a surface effect but an integral part of the finishing. It penetrates the fibre structure of the braid and makes it abrasion-resistant and dirt-resistant. A waxed LACCICO lace is also water-repellent and weatherproof, which extends the life of the cotton fibres. Visually, this process gives a silky-sheen finish that lends your shoes a refined expression.

detailsSettings.label: What are the benefits of the waxing?

text.htmlDescription: That depends mainly on the shoe. Waxed cotton is tear-resistant, and the wax protects it against moisture and abrasion. Premature wear usually comes from eyelets with burrs or from pulling in the wrong direction on hooks. If you look after your laces now and then, you will enjoy them for a long time.

detailsSettings.label: How long do LACCICO shoelaces last?

text.htmlDescription: Choosing the right lace

LACCICO length guide (rule of thumb for classic footwear)

The right length matters for both fit and look. As a rule of thumb for classic footwear, count the pairs of eyelets:

  • 1–2 pairs of eyelets: 45 cm
  • 3–4 pairs of eyelets: 60 cm
  • 4–5 pairs of eyelets: 75 cm (with Derby lacing, from 5 pairs of eyelets possibly 90 cm, depending on the foot)
  • 5–6 pairs of eyelets: 90 cm
  • 7–8 pairs of eyelets: 120 cm
  • 9+ pairs of eyelets / boots: 150 to 180 cm

Master's tip: If in doubt, measure your old laces unlaced. That way you get a good fit that matches your preferences exactly.

More on our Shoelace length page.

detailsSettings.label: What length do I need for my shoes?

text.htmlDescription:
Choosing between round and flat laces is a question of style and purpose. Every LACCICO model follows a shape-retaining logic:

  • R series (round laces R2, R3): The classic for business shoes and fine footwear. Understated, refined and supple.

  • F series (flat laces F3, F4, F6): Ideal for sneakers or sporty low shoes. They lie flat, are tear-resistant and give the shoe a striking look.

  • SL series (Splendore): Our finest finish – with a particularly silky sheen for a glamorous appearance on formal occasions.

  • XR series (Xtra Robust): For boots and heavy footwear. The soft yet solid feel is particularly resilient and grippy.

detailsSettings.label: Round or flat? The model series at a glance.

text.htmlDescription:
These two series mark the two ends of our range and show the breadth of what craftsmanship can do.

  • SL (Splendore di Laccico): This series is our finest finish. It stands out with a particularly silky shimmer and is designed for a glamorous appearance on formal occasions. Here the braid structure is fine, yet shape-retaining.

  • XR (Xtra Robust): Developed for heavy footwear and boots. What makes it special is the soft yet solid feel. These laces are noticeably resilient and, thanks to their dense construction, particularly grippy – ideal for heavy footwear off-road or at work.

detailsSettings.label: What distinguishes the SL and XR series?

text.htmlDescription:
Colour is an expression of character. In our range you will find over 50 shades, which I as a master shoemaker have selected specifically for different types of leather and styles. Use our colour filter to find the right group with confidence:

  • Classic tones: For a timeless, harmonious look in which the lace blends discreetly with the upper leather.

  • Contrast colours: If you want to make an authentic statement and strikingly emphasise the lines of your shoe.

The high colour fastness of our laces comes from the use of high-quality thoroughly dyed yarns. With normal wear, the colours therefore stay stable for a long time. Even if the surface becomes more matt over time through daily use, the colour substance in the core of the braid remains stable. How you can easily refresh the sheen when needed is explained in our care tips.

text.htmlDescription: Care & use

As cotton is a plant fibre, the material changes over time: weather and mechanical abrasion during lacing make the surface more porous, and the original sheen fades. This is not a quality defect, but a natural process with authentic waxed products.


Master's tip for refreshing the sheen:


You can extend the life of the cotton fibres by refreshing the laces from time to time. To do this, unthread the laces and pull them through a cloth on which you have put a small amount of wax-based shoe cream.

For flat laces there is another proven trick: by briefly smoothing them with a household iron – on a higher heat, as you would use for a T-shirt or jeans – the wax remaining in the lace becomes fluid again. It redistributes and soaks back into the braid where it was lost through use. This smooths the structure again; the lace stays supple and tear-resistant for a long time and keeps its high-quality look.

Important note: please note that wax residue may stick to the soleplate of the iron. Clean the soleplate carefully with a soft cloth and a suitable cleaner that reliably removes wax residue before using the iron again for light-coloured textiles or white laundry.

detailsSettings.label: How do I care for my waxed shoelaces?

text.htmlDescription:
It is a common misconception that the material alone is responsible for how well a bow holds. A correctly tied bow – technically a reef knot with two slipped loops – holds all day and even tightens itself under load, regardless of the material.


If a bow slips, it is usually due to the symmetry of the knot. Many people unknowingly tie the so-called “granny knot”, which sits crooked and loosens with movement.


Master's tip for the perfect bow:


Often all it takes is a tiny change to the starting knot: simply make your usual first cross the other way round (if you have always crossed left over right, now cross right over left) and then tie the bow as you always do.


This simple change creates a genuine, self-locking reef knot. The bow now lies straight on the shoe and no longer comes loose. A small advantage of waxed laces: when wet, the bow does not come undone as easily.

text.htmlDescription: Ordering & shipping

Your order is handed over to our shipping partner no later than the next working day (Monday to Friday) after receipt of payment. Within Germany, delivery usually takes 1 to 3 working days by letter post or as a small parcel. These shipping methods are particularly convenient, as delivery is usually made straight to your letterbox and you do not have to be at home to receive it.


For deliveries abroad we use the goods shipment service (Warensendung). To give you maximum security, this shipment always comes with tracking and proof of delivery. This way you can follow the journey of your new shoelaces at any time.

detailsSettings.label: How quickly will my order be delivered?

text.htmlDescription:
Which payment options are available to me?


In our online shop we offer all common and secure payment methods. You can pay conveniently by PayPal, credit card or via the usual instant payment systems. As soon as we have received your payment, we prepare your goods for shipping, which takes place no later than the next working day (Monday to Friday).


How long do I have to return an item?


We want you to be completely happy with your choice. We therefore offer you a voluntary right of return of 30 days in total from receipt of the goods. Within this period you can send the unused laces back to us in their original packaging if the colour or model does not suit your shoe perfectly.


Do you offer exchanges?


We do not offer a direct exchange (item for item). This route is often slow in terms of bookkeeping and delays the arrival of your new goods. It is easier and quicker for you: send the unsuitable item back to us as a return and simply order the item you want again directly in the shop. That way you receive your new laces without waiting, and we can refund your return as soon as we receive it.


How does the return work?


Every delivery includes a delivery note on which you will also find the address for returns. To speed up processing, please use this delivery note as a covering letter:


  • Partial return: Simply cross out by hand the items you are keeping.

  • Full return: Simply enclose the delivery note with the parcel.

If you no longer have the delivery note, a handwritten note of your order ID (order number from the confirmation e-mail) enclosed with the return is enough. That way we can assign your return immediately, even without a printer.


Why do the laces have to be unused?


As waxed shoelaces have a delicate finish, even threading them once leaves marks of use on the waxing. We therefore ask for your understanding that we can only accept returns in unused condition and in their original packaging. The cost of the return is borne by you as the buyer.


Who pays for the return shipping?


So that we can offer you our high-quality products at a fair price, you as the buyer bear the direct costs of the return. As soon as the return has arrived and been checked, we refund the purchase price via the payment method you originally chose.

text.htmlDescription: Good to know & technical details

How long a shoelace lasts depends largely on the condition of the metal parts on the shoe. When buying shoes, check that the hooks and eyelets have no sharp burrs. These often arise during production, when metal parts are attached with high pressure by pressing tools.


Such burrs are often hard for laypeople to spot. The clearest sign of such a defect on the shoe is a lace that wears out early or chafes through at one specific spot. In this case it is enough to remove the burr once. Connoisseurs of fine footwear can carefully smooth these sharp edges with very fine sandpaper (grit no coarser than 400). If you do not feel able to do this on the shoe yourself, we recommend visiting a shoemaker you trust. Smooth guidance protects the cotton fibres and considerably extends the life of your LACCICO laces.

detailsSettings.label: What should I look out for with the hooks and eyelets on my shoes?

text.htmlDescription:
After braiding, our shoelaces are stored on large reels. Finishing – that is, cutting to length and sealing the ends at the same time – takes place in one step on the so-called tipping machine.


The high working speed when unwinding from the reel creates mechanical tension. At that moment the braid is stretched very slightly. As soon as the finished lace rests relaxed after cutting and tipping, the braid returns to its original resting form. When measured in a completely relaxed state, there may therefore be slight production-related tolerances. However, this physical property of the construction has no influence on the quality or the fit on the shoe.

detailsSettings.label: Why do the actual lengths sometimes differ slightly?

text.htmlDescription: A short guide to hooks and eyelets

Which shoelace suits which hardware?Choosing the right lace depends not only on the style of the shoe, but also on the type of eyelets and hooks:

  • Concealed eyelets (blind eyelets): They almost always have an inner diameter of 3 mm. Here we recommend our fine round laces (R2) or narrow flat laces (F3). They glide through effortlessly and underline the elegance of business shoes.

  • Visible eyelets: On sneakers, boots and lace-up ankle boots you can see the metal ring on the outside. From 4 mm inner diameter, our 4 mm flat lace (F4) and the stronger round lace (R3) show to good advantage, from 5 mm inner diameter the 6 mm flat lace (F6) as well.

  • Speed hooks: On boots with open hooks on the shaft, a robust lace is the best choice. Our XR (Xtra Robust) flat laces are particularly popular here, as their soft yet solid construction makes them particularly resilient and they sit firmly in the hook without slipping.

Our waxed cotton laces are designed for a long life. Even so, there are physical limits: a very wide flat lace (F6) in an eyelet that is too small and sharp-edged is put under unnecessary strain. Make sure the lace always passes easily through the eyelet. Only if it can glide freely can the shoe be laced evenly, which both increases comfort and protects the material.
